newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala coffee exports down in September.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala coffee exports down in September.

text.p: Guatemalan coffee exports in September were 98,772 60-kilo bags, down 61 percent from the same month last year, the National Coffee Association (Anacafe) said on Friday.
"The September exports show a downhill trend in volume," Max Quirin, president of Anacafe, told Reuters.
Last September, Guatemala exported 251,879 bags. September 1996 exports were also 37 percent lower than the 157,662 60-kilo bags exported in August this year.
Guatemalan exports during the last quarter of coffee year 1995-1996 were 446,107 bags compared to 882,449 in the same period last year, said Quirin.
Exports have been down in Guatemala for several months because 90 percent of the 1995-1996 harvest had been sold by June.
The Anacafe president said delivery of the new crop to exporters has been delayed around a month because heavy rains in recent weeks have delayed ripening.
"The harvest has started but volumes of ripe beans are very low. They are picking much less coffee than what is normally expected in September because of the humidity and little heat," said Quirin.
